title: State of the meta per class and spec on Forever
about: Per class and spec on WoW: Forever: how each spec stands (levelling, groups, level 60), a short state-of-the-meta summary, stat priority, the enchants per slot with their spell ids, consumables, professions, gear priorities and the dated class changes since launch; sourced and summarised in our own words, complementing classes.json.

statements.title: Levelling default, mid-pack at 60
statements.text: Arms is still the spec most guides level in. At 60 it sits in the middle: MythicSim's single-target sim of 18 Nov puts it 18th of 24 DPS specs, and MeinMMO says its rage runs dry too often to stay near the top and that bleed-immune bosses hurt it badly. Warcraft Tavern sees its talents leaning toward PvP.

statements.title: The cleave DPS, weaker solo
statements.text: Fury is the warrior's group DPS spec. Blizzard told MeinMMO it should own fights against several tanked enemies, MythicSim ranks it 9th single target, and Wowhead calls it unmatched at low-target cleave but not a strong leveller: it needs other people around.

statements.title: Main tank, and a fine grinder
statements.text: Protection is the pick for main tanking: MeinMMO rates warriors the best main tanks of Forever and MythicSim has it second for threat behind the bear. Kami Labs adds that it levels well too, since Legacy talents and the new enchants give passive healing between packs.

statements.title: Arms in short
statements.text: Arms is how most warriors get to 60: one big, slow two-hander, bleeds, and Overpower whenever it lights up. It shines against two or three targets with Sweeping Strikes and Whirlwind, but in long single-target fights it trails Fury because its rage comes from slow swings. Gear for hit (to about 8%) and expertise first, then crit and Strength. Since 10 Nov Sweeping Strikes keeps its charges when no second target is hit.

statements.title: Fury in short
statements.text: Fury is the warrior to bring to a group: dual-wield, crit for rage, Whirlwind and Cleave on every pack. It is at its best when a tank holds several enemies in one place and weaker alone, so most level as Arms and switch later. Weapon skill and hit come first, then crit and Strength. Since 16 Nov Cleave and Heroic Strike trigger Unbridled Wrath and Reckless Swings and no longer eat Flurry charges.

statements.title: Protection in short
statements.text: Protection is the sturdiest tank in the game, built around a shield: Defensive Stance threat went up to 80% before launch and Shield Slam and Bastion want a shield equipped. It also grinds packs well thanks to Legacy talents and healing enchants. Balance survival (Stamina, armour, avoidance) with enough hit, Strength and crit to hold threat.

statements.title: Blacksmithing first
statements.text: Blacksmithing plus Mining is the usual warrior pair: Blacksmithing makes plate and mail, much of it only for smiths. Engineering is the other pick for its gadgets.

statements.title: Slow two-hander first
statements.text: The weapon is the biggest upgrade: a slow, hard-hitting two-hander for Mortal Strike, Overpower and Slam. Plate is ideal but there is no penalty for mail or leather with better stats; the ranged slot is only a stat stick.

statements.title: Two one-handers, slow main hand
statements.text: Dual-wield with the slowest strong main hand you can find; armour type matters less than the stats.

statements.title: Always a shield, plate from 40
statements.text: Tank in mail until 40 and plate after; dropping an armour class hurts mitigation. Always carry a shield (Bastion and Shield Slam need one). Blacksmithing shield spikes add damage per block.

statements.title: Forceful armour kits
statements.text: Leatherworking's Forceful armour kits (attack power plus armour) go on chest, legs, hands or feet and often give more for the gold than an enchant on gear you keep.

statements.title: 16 Nov: Cleave and Heroic Strike fixed for Fury
statements.text: Cleave and Heroic Strike now trigger Unbridled Wrath and Reckless Swings and no longer use up Flurry charges, so queuing them no longer costs Fury its haste.

statements.title: 10 Nov: Sweeping Strikes keeps charges
statements.text: Sweeping Strikes no longer spends its charges on hits that find no second target.

statements.title: 13 Nov: Berserker Rage breaks Sap
statements.text: Berserker Rage now removes Sap, as it was meant to.

statements.title: 3 Nov: launch tuning for warriors
statements.text: Before launch Defensive Stance threat went to +80%, Two-Handed Weapon Specialization to 2/4/6% and Flurry became a 3-point talent; Blizzard also raised class damage across the board and gave higher-level mobs more health to match.

statements.title: Strong leveller, A tier at 60
statements.text: Retribution is one of launch's big winners: Kami Labs calls it very easy and very strong to level, AoE farming included, and MythicSim puts it 4th of 24 DPS specs on 18 Nov. MeinMMO is more careful (solid, best against undead and demons) and expects hybrids to sit 5-10% under pure DPS by design.

statements.title: The AoE tank
statements.text: Protection was so strong in the beta that it took nerfs and is still one of the best dungeon tanks and gold grinders, per Kami Labs. MeinMMO rates it the best tank on many targets, Wowhead the strongest against magic damage. MythicSim's single-target threat test puts it last of the standard tanks.

statements.title: The single-target healer
statements.text: Holy is seen as the biggest single-target healer with near-endless mana (Kami Labs) and the most efficient one (MeinMMO), and every group wants a paladin's blessings. It levels smoothly thanks to self-healing and plate.

statements.title: Retribution in short
statements.text: Ret is one of Forever's winners: easy to level, strong at AoE farming, and high in the 60 simulations. The build is a slow two-hander with Seal of Command and Holy Strike, and Intellect now feeds spell damage through Champion of the Light. Weapon damage and speed come first, then hit and expertise, then spell damage and Intellect ahead of Strength. Judgements count as ranged attacks since 11 Nov, except Judgement of Command, which is melee again since 13 Nov.

statements.title: Protection in short
statements.text: Protection paladins tank big pulls with Consecration and Holy Shield and are hard to kill with magic. Blizzard wants spell power to be their main damage stat: since 17 Nov the Soulforge tank set carries spell power instead of Strength. Hit, spell power and Stamina lead the stat list. Mana is the limit on long pulls.

statements.title: Holy in short
statements.text: Holy is the plain, efficient tank healer: big cast-time heals, crits that pay back mana, and the class's blessings and auras for the group. Stack healing power, then Intellect, then crit and Spirit. It levels better than in Classic since it has its own healing and sturdy armour, but kills slowly alone.

statements.title: Retribution stat priority
statements.text: Hit, expertise, strength, attack power, spell damage, intellect, crit, agility. Caps: hit to 9%, expertise to 6.5%. About half put spell damage above attack power; some put intellect above spell damage; some put crit above intellect.

statements.title: Protection stat priority
statements.text: Hit, defense, stamina, spell damage, armor, avoidance, strength, crit, agility. Start balanced between the defensive and offensive picks. About half put defense above hit; about half put stamina above defense; about half put spell damage above stamina.

statements.title: Holy stat priority
statements.text: Healing power, intellect, crit, spirit, mp5. Some put spirit above crit; some put mp5 above spirit.

statements.title: Blacksmithing first

statements.title: Slow two-hander first
statements.text: A slow two-hander with high weapon DPS beats almost any other stat line, since Holy Strike, Seal of Command and white hits scale with it. Pick a libram whose effect fits your rotation.

statements.title: Weapon DPS versus spell power
statements.text: Weapon DPS matters but caster weapons trade it for spell power; mail until 40, plate after. Leatherworking's Mystic kits (spell power and armour) fit the chest, legs, hands and feet.

statements.title: Caster stats over armour
statements.text: Holy takes healing stats over armour type, so cloth or leather pieces are fine; one-hander plus shield, since paladins cannot use staves.

statements.title: 17 Nov: Soulforge set gets spell power
statements.text: The upgraded tank Dungeon Set Soulforge Armor swapped Strength for Intellect and spell power; Blizzard says spell power is meant to be the paladin tank's damage stat.

statements.title: 19 Nov: Two-Handed Weapon Specialization fixed
statements.text: Two-Handed Weapon Specialization now raises all Holy damage while a two-hander is equipped.

statements.title: 11 Nov: Unsealed Fury and Windfury
statements.text: Unsealed Fury no longer makes echoes from Windfury Totem attacks, after Windfury started triggering from Holy Strike.

statements.title: 11-13 Nov: Judgements are ranged, except Command
statements.text: Since 11 Nov Judgements count as ranged attacks (ranged hit chance, no melee procs). On 13 Nov Judgement of Command went back to being a melee attack that triggers on-hit effects.

statements.title: Top leveller, still A tier at 60
statements.text: Beast Mastery is the easiest levelling spec in the game: the pet tanks and pets now take the hunter's stats. At 60 it is third in MythicSim's DPS sim of 18 Nov, and wow.gg's tier list has the three hunter specs as the top damage dealers. It brings no raid buff of its own.

statements.title: Second-best DPS in the sims
statements.text: Marksmanship is second in MythicSim's single-target sim (81% of Survival). It can drop the pet for more personal damage; Trueshot Aura now covers the raid but lost its melee attack power.

statements.title: Top of the DPS sims, harder to level
statements.text: Survival is the top DPS spec in every MythicSim snapshot since October; wow.gg and MeinMMO agree hunters lead the damage charts. Kami Labs expects that to come down. It is a melee-weaving spec that only really works from about 30, so few level in it.

statements.title: Beast Mastery in short
statements.text: Hunters are the class to beat on Forever, and BM is the comfortable way to get there: the pet tanks and pets now take the hunter's stats, so it solos what others cannot. At 60 it stays in A tier for damage with a simple rotation. Hit to 8% first, then crit, Agility and Intellect. Since 10 Nov pets have 115% of normal health (a bug had given 150%).

statements.title: Marksmanship in short
statements.text: Marksmanship hits harder itself and can go petless for even more damage, which puts it second in the 60 simulations. The trade-off is positioning and threat, since no pet holds the mobs. Same stats as BM: hit to 8%, crit, Agility, Intellect. Volley no longer triggers procs and stops when you move (11 Nov).

statements.title: Survival in short
statements.text: Survival came back as a melee hybrid: weave melee into shots or go full melee with a two-hander, a very high attack speed and Rapid Fire that works in melee. It tops the damage sims but is hard to play and only comes together around 30. Hit, crit, Agility, then Strength and attack power.

statements.title: 10 Nov: pets back to 115% health, Arcane Shot cost
statements.text: Pets had 150% of their intended health by mistake; it is 115% now. Arcane Shot and Summon Hawk cost 11% of base mana at every rank, and the Hawk's melee damage went up about 80%.

statements.title: 6 Nov: Blizzard on pet durability
statements.text: Blizzard wanted hunter pets to tank about as well as in Classic Era. The Nov 10 hotfix set pet health to 115% of normal after a bug had raised it to 150%.

statements.title: 11 Nov: Volley fixed

statements.title: 3 Nov: launch shot buffs
statements.text: Before launch Aimed Shot bonus damage rose about 110%, Arcane Shot about 30% with a higher attack power coefficient, and Serpent Sting scaled better.

statements.title: The levelling and PvE workhorse
statements.text: Combat is the most played rogue spec and the usual way to level. At 60 it is a B-tier spec in MythicSim (16th), but Blizzard told MeinMMO rogues should be the best single-target damage, and Blade Flurry makes Combat good on several targets too.

statements.title: Strongest rogue spec on one target
statements.text: Assassination was rebuilt around poisons and Mutilate. Wowhead calls it the strongest rogue spec for single-target damage, and MythicSim has it as the top rogue (10th, A tier). It only comes online with Venom and Mutilate, so it is not a starter spec.

statements.title: PvP first
statements.text: Subtlety is the control spec for PvP and world PvP. MeinMMO does not expect it to compete in PvE; MythicSim has it 15th, just ahead of Combat. It can level (bleed or Ambush builds) but takes longer.

statements.title: Combat in short
statements.text: Combat is the safe rogue: it levels with any weapon (axes and maces now count, via Hack and Slash) and cleaves with Blade Flurry. Blizzard wants rogues on top for single-target damage, so expect the class to be pushed up if it lags. Hit to 8% and expertise come first, then weapon skill and poison hit, then Agility and crit. The main-hand weapon is the biggest upgrade by far.

statements.title: Assassination in short
statements.text: Assassination is now a real poison spec: poisons can crit and scale with attack power, and Mutilate plus Venom turn daggers into the strongest single-target rogue build. It is fiddly and gear-hungry, so level as Combat and switch around 40. Same stat order as Combat, with hit to 17% worth more because poisons need it.

statements.title: Subtlety in short
statements.text: Subtlety has two builds now, bleeds or dagger Ambush crits, and owns PvP control. In PvE it trails the other two. Same stats as the other rogues; daggers for the Ambush build.

statements.title: 3 Nov: launch rogue rework
statements.text: Before launch rogues got Shank (level 24), doubled poison attack power scaling, a stronger Mutilate and the Death Mark talent; Dual Wield Specialization became 2 points for 25/50% off-hand damage.

statements.title: Levels fine, middle of the pack at 60
statements.text: Shadow is the usual levelling spec and can heal levelling dungeons without a respec. At 60 MythicSim puts it 22nd of 24 DPS specs; MeinMMO calls it a solid middle that brings support, and Kami Labs a group mana battery thanks to Dark Inspiration and Vampiric Embrace.

statements.title: Tank healer, safe solo
statements.text: Discipline is the shield and tank-healing spec. Wowhead sees it as a possible raid staple and a great dungeon healer that still solos with a wand; MeinMMO rates it a little under Holy because Holy can take most of its best shield talents.

statements.title: The group healer, top of the healer picks
statements.text: Holy is the healer most lists put first: wow.gg names it the best healer, MeinMMO credits it with the strongest group heals, and Kami Labs counts it among the two best area healers with Restoration druids. Too slow to level alone.

statements.title: Shadow in short
statements.text: Shadow is the comfortable solo priest and a solid group DPS that also feeds the party mana (Dark Inspiration) and healing (Vampiric Embrace). It is not a top damage spec at 60. Hit to 17%, then crit and shadow damage, then Intellect. Since 16 Nov Vampiric Embrace heals the party for half as much (the priest's own healing is unchanged) and Dark Inspiration no longer stacks between Shadow priests.

statements.title: Discipline in short
statements.text: Discipline is the tank healer with shields, Penance and Power Infusion, one of the strongest buffs you can give another player. It levels safely with shield, Shadow Word: Pain and a wand. Healing power, then Intellect and Spirit, then crit.

statements.title: Holy in short
statements.text: Holy is the raid and group healer: Prayer of Mending, Binding Heal and Holy Nova make it the best area healer on most lists. Healing power first, then Intellect, mp5 and Spirit. It needs a group to level.

statements.title: Strong leveller, A tier at 60
statements.text: Enhancement is the levelling spec, and Wowhead calls it a very strong one since it lives off weapon swings, not mana. At 60 MythicSim has it 11th (A tier) after the 10 Nov nerfs; MeinMMO expects big burst but less over long fights, offset by its totems.

statements.title: Weak on one target, good at AoE
statements.text: Elemental is the weakest shaman spec at 60 on paper: MythicSim puts it 19th, MeinMMO calls it one of the worst in the beta. Wowhead sees good cleave and AoE but mediocre single target.

statements.title: Every raid wants one
statements.text: Restoration is in demand for its totems, Mana Tide and tank healing (MeinMMO), and Wowhead rates its endgame potential strong. Levelling as Restoration only makes sense in a steady group.

statements.title: Enhancement in short
statements.text: Enhancement levels fast on a slow two-hander and brings Windfury and other totems to every group. The November patch moved it back to Strength: Stormstrike now hits for 100% weapon damage every 8 seconds, Mental Dexterity converts less Intellect, and Maelstrom Weapon procs more often on slow weapons. Gear for hit, expertise, crit and Strength, not caster pieces. Weapon imbues and weapon totems now work at the same time.

statements.title: Elemental in short
statements.text: Elemental had a rough beta and still sims low on one target, though Lava Burst, Lightning Overload and big crits make it fun and strong in PvP and on packs. Its end-game stats are spell penetration, haste, hit to 17% and spell damage, with Intellect and Spirit for mana. Most level as Enhancement and pick this up as a second spec.

statements.title: Restoration in short
statements.text: Restoration heals with Riptide and Chain Heal, both stronger than in Classic, and Mindfulness eases mana. Its totems make it welcome everywhere and it is a good tank healer. Healing, crit, haste, Intellect, Spirit, mp5. Keep it as the second spec rather than levelling in it.

statements.text: Weapon damage and speed come first; after the November update Maelstrom Weapon procs more per swing on slow weapons. Blizzard wants Strength to be the best stat, so collect Strength and attack power gear, not caster gear.

statements.title: 10 Nov: Enhancement back on Strength
statements.text: Stormstrike went to 100% weapon damage on an 8 s cooldown (was 150% / 6 s), Mental Dexterity to 33/66/100% of Intellect, and Maelstrom Weapon to a flat 20% per stack with fewer, speed-based procs. Blizzard's goal: Strength over Intellect and spell power.

statements.title: 16-17 Nov: Maelstrom and Windfury fixes
statements.text: One Maelstrom Weapon proc now helps only one cast, Thundering Strikes works without a weapon, and Windfury Totem attacks no longer eat Flurry charges.

statements.title: 10 Nov: imbues and totems together

statements.title: Levelling and PvP spec
statements.text: Frost is how most mages level: slows, freezes and Ice Barrier keep it safe. At 60 MythicSim puts it last of the mages (23rd of 24), and Kami Labs and MeinMMO see Fire and Arcane ahead for damage, with Frost strongest in PvP.

statements.title: Slow start, scales with gear
statements.text: Fire levels badly but scales: MeinMMO expects it to start weaker and end strong, MythicSim has it 14th today. Wowhead has not settled between Deep Fire and Frostfire builds.

statements.title: The burst spec everyone talks about
statements.text: Arcane, with the new Arcane Wrath, is the spec Kami Labs expects to dominate and possibly be nerfed. MythicSim has it 13th, just ahead of Fire; MeinMMO credits it with the best short burst but warns it runs dry in long fights.

statements.title: Frost in short
statements.text: Frost is the safe way to level a mage and the PvP pick at 60. Ice Lance and Fingers of Frost now make Shatter work on bosses too, but in the 60 simulations Frost still trails Fire and Arcane. Hit up to 11-12% (talents give the rest), then crit, spell damage and Intellect. Since 13 Nov damage from procs and Blizzard breaks Frost Nova, so don't Blizzard what you just rooted.

statements.title: Fire in short
statements.text: Fire is the gear-hungry scaler: weak while levelling, strong once crit is high, with Heating Up to speed Pyroblast. Improved Scorch now only buffs your own fire damage. Hit to 17%, spell damage and fire damage, then crit, spell penetration and haste.

statements.title: Arcane in short
statements.text: Arcane is the burst mage: Arcane Wrath and Arcane Blast hit very hard, Missile Barrage adds free missiles, and it levels decently with Clearcasting and mana regen. Long fights drain it, so it depends on how fast your group kills. Hit to 17%, spell damage, crit, spell penetration, haste, Intellect.

statements.title: Burst and AoE

statements.text: Affliction levels on DoTs and drains and stays a strong raid spec, with Wrack as the channel that speeds up your DoT ticks. Spell power and shadow damage first, then crit, hit (12% from gear with 5/5 Suppression) and haste.

statements.text: Restoration is a top area healer now (Kami Labs) with Wild Growth, Swiftmend and HoTs that crit; MeinMMO calls it far more valuable than in Classic, at the cost of overhealing.

statements.text: Feral is the flexible druid: cat for questing and damage, bear for bad pulls and tanking, and Forever finally makes feral scale with weapon damage, so a hard-hitting two-hander and weapon stones matter. The bear tops the threat sims and the cat sits in A tier. Crit, hit to 8%, expertise, haste, then weapon DPS and Agility or Strength. Hit to 17%, spell damage, spell penetration, crit, haste. Fine for levelling after 30 with Entangling Roots now hitting several targets.

statements.title: 3 Nov: launch feral buffs

Windfury Totem can proc from any melee ability, but off-hand strikes from abilities such as Whirlwind or Mutilate cannot; only their main-hand strike can.
One Maelstrom Weapon proc can only benefit a single cast.
Windfury Totem attacks no longer consume Flurry stacks.
Mental Dexterity now converts 33/66/100% of Intellect into attack power (was 50/100/150%).

Warriors have a Weaponmaster talent that improves whichever weapon type they use, so they need no respec when switching weapons.
Paladin Consecration was heavily weakened compared with Classic.

Mage-only quest Rituals of Power (level 30, not shareable): a breadcrumb from any city mage trainer leads to Tabetha in Dustwallow, then Magus Tirth in Thousand Needles. The book is at the end of Scarlet Monastery Library.
Early warrior gear priority while levelling: weapon DPS, then Strength or attack power, Stamina, Agility, armour.
Levelling Arms values the weapon's hit damage above its DPS, then Strength or attack power, Stamina, Agility, armour.

For levelling Arms, Bloodthrill is the talent that makes the spec work. Spearing Strike only pays off against Giants and Dragonkin, so it can be skipped early to max Two-Handed Weapon Specialization sooner.
Protection levelling clears packs with little health lost. Priority: Shield Slam, Revenge when it lights up, Rend on targets that live, Thunder Clap on cooldown, Heroic Strike with spare rage.
Fury levels dual-wielding with Bloodthirst then Whirlwind, Overpower only when already in Battle Stance. It takes a lot of damage, so expect downtime between pulls.
Warriors learn Dual Talent Specialization from their class trainer at level 40.

Defensive Stance lowers damage taken and dealt and raises threat. Berserker Stance raises crit chance and damage taken. Battle Stance has no passive bonus.
Warriors should spend Retaliation, Shield Wall and Intimidating Shout freely to pull more mobs at once rather than saving them, since idle cooldowns cost levelling speed.
Health potions can be crafted with First Aid.
Cooking skill is needed to set up your own campsite.

contradictions.title: Is Frost a competitive PvE spec?
contradictions.text: Warcraft Tavern's Frost guide says Ice Lance and Fingers of Frost made Frost a highly competitive PvE spec. MythicSim (18 Nov) puts it last of the mages, and Kami Labs and MeinMMO both see Fire and Arcane ahead for damage. Follow the sims for group damage at 60; Frost stays the safe levelling and PvP pick.

contradictions.title: Elemental after the beta buffs
contradictions.text: Kami Labs says Elemental was hugely buffed late in the beta after a joke start; MeinMMO still calls it one of the worst and says the sims stay poor, and MythicSim has it 19th. Follow the sims: still below average on one target.

contradictions.title: Which tank is best?
contradictions.text: wow.gg and MythicSim's threat test put the Feral bear first; MeinMMO calls warriors the best main tanks, paladins the best on many targets and bears the best off-tanks. MythicSim measures threat only, not survival, so both can hold: bear for threat, warrior for a main tank.

contradictions.title: Shadow: crit or spell power after hit?
contradictions.text: Wowhead puts spell crit above shadow damage after the 17% hit cap; Warcraft Tavern puts spell power above crit. Both agree hit comes first. Either order is close; Wowhead is the more recent page.

contradictions.title: Enhancement: where does Intellect go?
contradictions.text: Wowhead's 16 Nov list still ranks Intellect right after Strength; Blizzard's 6 Nov intent is Strength first and no preference for caster gear, and the November patch cut the Intellect conversion. Follow Blizzard: Strength and attack power gear, Intellect only as a bonus.

contradictions.title: Retribution: Strength or spell power?
contradictions.text: Warcraft Tavern ranks Strength and attack power above Intellect and spell power; Wowhead (31 Oct) puts spell damage and Intellect above Strength, since Champion of the Light turns Intellect into spell damage. Both put weapon damage and hit first. Treat it as open until level-60 data settles.

contradictions.title: Holy Paladin as a raid healer
contradictions.text: Wowhead's pre-raid tier list, relayed by JudgeHype, ranks Holy last of the healers (C-tier). The KB's Holy standing, from Kami Labs and MeinMMO, calls it the strongest single-target and most mana-efficient healer. Both are forecasts until raids open; the first raid weeks should settle it. This contradicts class-meta:paladin:holy:standing.

Level-60 rogue enchants and consumables beyond the levelling list (no flask or end-game weapon enchant named yet).

Elemental level-60 enchants and consumables: the Wowhead list only names the weapon enchant.
Spellblasting versus Mighty Spell Power on a staff at 60: Wowhead has not compared them on level-60 gear.

Feral cat enchants at 60: the cat list only names the weapon enchant and armour kits; the bracketed list is the bear one.
